When any non-SMS workflow reminder has retryCount > 1, the deleteMany second OR branch matches it regardless of method, causing email or WhatsApp reminders to be deleted by the SMS cron run. The retry cleanup must remain scoped to SMS reminders by adding method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the second OR branch, or by combining the method predicate outside the OR.

Unguarded retryCount update in catch can abort the whole cron run - when twilio.scheduleSMS throws and the prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block also throws, the exception escapes the loop, causing the cron request to fail and later reminders to be skipped.

Retry count is not incremented when message or sendTo is missing - when sendTo or message is empty, the outer if is skipped and retryCount is never incremented, causing the reminder to be retried on every cron run until its scheduled date, defeating the retry limit.

When two cron requests process the same unscheduled reminder concurrently, both iterations read the same reminder.retryCount and write the same incremented value, so the failure count is lost and the reminder can be sent/retried beyond the two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment: 1 update and add a claim/lock before scheduling to prevent concurrent processing.

Failure after a successful scheduleSMS is counted as a retry and can cause a duplicate SMS - when twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but the following prisma.workflowReminder.update setting scheduled: true throws, the catch block increments retryCount, leaving the reminder unscheduled to be scheduled again on the next run.

Process reuse is based only on pgrep -f substring match and URL from shared fixed log /tmp/tmole.log, which may be stale, belong to another session, or not exist, potentially writing another session's public URL into GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL

In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts, forEach launches async deletions without awaiting them, so Reschedule sends the reschedule email and returns before the old calendar or video events are deleted; rejections bypass the try/catch block.

In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, async callback passed to forEach yields at await getCalendar(credential), so Promise.all over apiDeletes runs before any apiDeletes.push calls and the handler returns while calendar deletions are still running.

In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, forEach starts async deletions without awaiting them, so Reschedule sends the reschedule email and returns before the old external events are removed; deletion failures become unhandled promise rejections.

In packages/app-store/index.ts, every import() expression in the appStore object executes immediately when the module is evaluated, so all 28 integrations start loading regardless of which provider is needed, adding startup cost and potentially failing startup. Should use deferred loaders (functions returning import()).

Working-hours check compares slot start with itself and rejects slots covered by another range - when a weekday has multiple working-hour ranges, checkIfIsAvailable rejects a slot as soon as any matching range does not contain it, filtering out valid slots with split ranges like 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00

When two fixed hosts have overrides on the same date, checkIfIsAvailable receives the flattened dateOverrides for every host and does not filter them by host, so an override belonging only to host B can set dateOverrideExist for host A and make A's slot pass outside A's actual override

When a slot starts before a working-hours closing time but extends past it, checkIfIsAvailable sets end to the slot start, so the closing-time comparison never detects the overrun and an unavailable booking time is returned

When a date override has equal start and end timestamps, checkIfIsAvailable compares two different Dayjs object instances with ===, so this branch is never taken and the override is processed as a normal interval

When a host has multiple date overrides on the same day, checkIfIsAvailable rejects a slot as soon as it falls outside any one override, even when it is inside another, because find searches for an outside interval rather than an interval that contains the slot

When the invitee timezone is not UTC, checkIfIsAvailable compares UTC day/minutes from slotStartTime with workingHours values expressed in the invitee/local day, causing slots near a day boundary to be rejected or matched against the wrong interval

Override offset parsing via Date.toString() and unguarded timezone/day wrap - when override.start is a Date, getSlots builds the offset from dayjs(override.start.toString()), a locale string that is re-parsed, and override.timeZone is optional so undefined produces wrong offset

When a flattened date override carries a timezone different from the schedule timezone passed as organizerTimeZone, checkIfIsAvailable derives the shift from the schedule timezone and ignores the override's stored timeZone

When an override crosses the invitee's calendar-day boundary, getSlots shifts the override only after activeOverrides has filtered it by the unshifted UTC date, so the override is omitted for the invitee day that actually contains it

When a date override spans a daylight-saving transition, getSlots applies the UTC-offset difference at override.start to both endpoints, so the converted endTime is wrong after the organizer or invitee changes offset during the override

When a slot starts exactly at a date override's end, checkIfIsAvailable treats it as inside the override because the condition only rejects strictly later starts, so a slot immediately after an override can be returned as available

test_installation_not_found uses a hardcoded state value that gets rejected by OAuthLoginView.dispatch at the state check before GitHubInstallation runs, so the test passes even if installation 404 handling regresses - should use the pipeline signature from the preceding initialization request and assert the endpoint was requested

OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls get_user_info without exception handling, so when GitHub's /user request fails or returns a non-mapping body, the exception propagates and user sees a 500 instead of the installation error page

GitHubInstallation.dispatch has unguarded access to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] which raises KeyError when an existing active Integration has no sender key in its metadata, resulting in a 500 instead of the invalid-request page

The queued field default value timezone.now() is evaluated once at class definition/import time, causing all AssignmentSource instances created after module import to share the same stale timestamp instead of getting the current time when instantiated

MetricAlertDetectorHandler is an empty pass subclass of StatefulDetectorHandler that leaves abstract hooks unimplemented, causing TypeError when instantiated via Detector.detector_handler instead of returning an empty list like the old stub
TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds expected occurrence with group key 'val1' while the result under test uses 'group_key', causing fingerprint mismatch and assertion failure
Partial failure at src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:56 can leave an environment in ERROR state without an active incident

Hung flusher process is never killed before restart - _ensure_processes_alive guards kill() with isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) but workers are SpawnProcess objects which are not instances of that class, so the check is False and hung processes are never killed, causing process leaks

When join(timeout=...) reaches its deadline while waiting for an earlier worker, the break exits the loop before later workers are terminated, leaving background processes alive after the strategy has returned - later workers are neither waited on nor terminated so flusher processes can outlive the strategy

When a produce_to_pipe flusher thread is detected as hung, _ensure_processes_alive skips termination because threading.Thread is not a multiprocessing.Process, then starts a replacement for the same shards, so both workers flush the same Redis keys and can publish duplicate payloads

Memory check scans the whole Redis cluster once per flusher buffer - when spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage is below 1.0, SpanFlusher.submit calls get_memory_info() on every per-process buffer, causing the memory query to run N times per submit and Redis INFO load to grow with the number of flusher processes

Strategy close()/terminate() shuts down the factory-owned shared queue pool - when arroyo closes or terminates a SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy during a rebalance, close() calls queue_pool.shutdown() on the pool owned by the factory, and the next strategy reuses the same dead pool causing put to raise and offsets to be marked complete, dropping results

When decoding, grouping, or queue_pool.submit raises, SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit logs the error and immediately completes the broker offset, so the message can be committed without ever being processed

Error-handling test asserts no commit, contradicting its docstring and the production code - test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts no offset was committed but the docstring says errors must not block commits, and it only passes due to timing before the 1s commit loop ticks

Failed items are marked complete, contradicting the 'only after successful processing' guarantee - when result_processor raises, OrderedQueueWorker.run logs the exception but still marks the offset complete in finally, causing the commit loop to commit past the failed item

A gap in submitted offsets stalls commits permanently - when a partition has an offset that is never submitted (like a transaction marker or compacted offset), the range loop in get_committable_offsets breaks at the gap and highest_committable never advances
test_preserves_order_within_group only checks that five results exist but doesn't verify ordering, so the test passes even if same-subscription messages are processed out of order

test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling assertion rejects the actual behavior where OrderedQueueWorker.run catches exceptions but still calls complete_offset in finally for both offsets, allowing the commit loop to commit offset 102

Unbounded queues contradict the documented backpressure - FixedQueuePool builds each queue with no maxsize, so SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit never blocks or rejects and the backlog grows without bound in memory

test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown only asserts that factory.queue_pool is None but doesn't verify graceful draining - queued results can be discarded unprocessed while the test still passes
test_concurrent_processing_across_groups only verifies eventual completion and group names but doesn't observe overlapping execution, so a serial implementation would satisfy this test

test_thread_queue_parallel_concurrent_subscriptions only waits for both calls to finish but doesn't measure overlap, so it passes without detecting if OrderedQueueWorker executes callbacks serially instead of concurrently

Denial-cache test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' passes even if the denial cache is ignored because it seeds permCache with false for dashboards:uid:dash1, which already denies access - contradicting the comment that it allows access, meaning a regression in the denial short-circuit would go undetected by CI

When a Check is denied before a resource is created or permission granted, the denial is cached and returned for up to 30 seconds (shortCacheTTL) even after the resource or grant exists - need to add invalidation for resource/permission mutations or avoid caching denials that can be changed by those operations

permDenialKey omits checkReq.IdentityType, so when a user and service account in the same namespace use the same UID string for the same resource, a denial cached for one identity incorrectly denies the other without evaluating its permissions - need to include identity type and canonical identifier in the denial key

When permission cache is populated before a dashboard or folder is created, List treats the cached scope map as complete and passes it to listPermission, so the new resource is omitted until cache expires - unlike Check, this path has no database fallback for stale cached permissions

When GrafanaRuleListItem supplies only promRule, AlertRuleMenu computes canPause and canDelete from Grafana prom abilities but menu items are still gated on rulerRule, so Pause and Delete actions are not rendered for users with those permissions

When AlertRuleMenu renders a data-source rule with skipToken, useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities receives undefined rule and useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading: false, causing Duplicate to be supported and potentially appear on cloud rules incorrectly

When GrafanaRuleListItem supplies only promRule, canSilence becomes true from Grafana ability hook but RuleActionsButtons.V2 caller's showSilenceDrawer branch requires rulerRule, so clicking Silence sets state without rendering any drawer

Federated-rule check dropped from legacy useAllAlertRuleAbilities path - useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false, so federated rules are no longer treated as immutable and edit/delete actions appear for rules that cannot be changed
Pause, Export, Restore and DeletePermanently are gated on isAlertingRule in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, which excludes Grafana recording rules that previously had these abilities

When Grafana Prometheus rule's folder is still loading or missing, useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities computes Silence from useCanSilenceInFolder which may fall back to global silence permission without requiring a loaded folder

When AlertRuleMenu is rendered for prom-only list item, useRulerRuleAbilities still runs useAllRulerRuleAbilities and useIsRuleEditable, triggering ruler feature-discovery requests contrary to the goal of removing ruler requests

Shard path interpolates each query twice - when runShardSplitQuery interpolates targets and passes them to splitQueriesByStreamShard, each shard sub-request goes through runSplitQuery which interpolates the same queries again, causing every shard request to get a second templateSrv.replace and ad hoc filter pass, which may duplicate filters or re-expand values
TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, causing log calls to be recorded on a discarded instance so assertions on the injected logger's InfoLogs see zero calls
ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData dereferences req.PluginContext without nil check, causing panic when nil request is passed instead of delegating to next
ContextualLoggerMiddleware.CallResource dereferences req without nil check, causing panic when nil request is passed
ContextualLoggerMiddleware.CheckHealth dereferences req without nil check, causing panic when nil request is passed
ContextualLoggerMiddleware.CollectMetrics dereferences req without nil check, causing panic when nil request is passed

When CreateOrUpdateDevice rejects a new device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, tagDeviceUI has already inserted its cache key before the database call, so the returned authentication error is bypassed on the next request from the same device and the request is accepted without rechecking the limit. Move the cache insertion after a successful store operation, or remove the key when tagging fails.

When frontend code reads anonymousDeviceLimit from GrafanaBootConfig, the property is initialized with = undefined, so it is inferred as type undefined rather than a number. The numeric limit the backend always sends (0 meaning unlimited) cannot be consumed with a correct type, and === undefined checks mishandle 0. Annotate the property as number | undefined.

When multiple requests call AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice concurrently while the active count is below deviceLimit, each request can observe the same count and then insert a device, so the configured cap is exceeded during concurrent anonymous authentication. Make the count-and-create operation atomic with a transaction, database constraint, or serialized locking strategy.

Device tagging moved onto the authentication request path - Authenticate now calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously instead of running in a goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout. Every anonymous request whose device is not in the local cache now waits on a COUNT query and an upsert, or on the updateDevice UPDATE, even when deviceLimit is 0.

When the first updateDevice execution returns a retryable database-lock error, WithDbSession invokes the callback again with args already prefixed by query, so this line prefixes it a second time and the retry executes with the wrong argument count. The lock retry then returns an error instead of applying the update. Build the argument slice once outside the callback or reset it before each execution.

CleanAnnotations calls r.log.Error before and after each delete even when err is nil, causing routine cleanups to emit error-level log entries that can trigger error alerting and dump whole ID lists into logs
Cleanup ticker interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, causing cleanup jobs to fire ten times more frequently and increasing database load

When AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize exceeds the database driver's parameter limit (2100 on MSSQL, 65535 on PostgreSQL/MySQL), deleteByIDs builds one placeholder per fetched ID causing the delete to fail with a bind/parameter-count error

When SQLite is configured with a very large AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, deleteByIDs interpolates every fetched ID into a single DELETE IN statement which can exceed SQLite's SQL length limit causing cleanup errors

Async legacy writes derive their context from the request context via context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...), so they are cancelled when the request ends, causing legacy and unified storage to silently diverge

DualWriterMode3.Update passes the original objInfo to the asynchronous legacy update, so an UpdatedObjectInfo that is context-dependent or single-use can be evaluated again and produce a different object from the one committed to unified storage

When the asynchronous legacy delete-collection finishes, DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection records its result with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, so legacy latency and failures are attributed to unified storage

When the unified-store create or update fails, DualWriterMode3 records that storage operation with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, so failure counts and latency are attributed to the wrong backend

Tests for DualWriterMode3.Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection only check the unified-store result and never synchronize or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, so tests pass even if the legacy write is skipped or fails

When multiple non-development requests arrive while the cache is empty, GetWebAssets waits for the first loader and then performs the file/CDN load again instead of using the cache that was just populated, causing redundant serialized I/O and latency. Need to re-read entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock and return it for non-development environments before loading.

enableSqlExpressions function ignores the feature flag and always returns false - operators who enable the sqlExpressions flag still get the error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' because the enabled variable is inverted

Stub DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go returns a generic 'not implemented' error from every method (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto), causing opaque errors for callers that bypass the reader gate and failing parser tests that expect table names
TotalDocs reads b.cache without cacheMu while builds now write it concurrently - Go can raise a fatal concurrent map read/write error and crash the process

Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same key - when two callers miss the cache for the same NamespacedResource concurrently, two indexes are built and the last write silently overwrites b.cache[key], leaking the other index

Reordered init now starts the watcher only after the full index build - s.search.init now runs before s.initWatcher(), causing server construction and process startup to stall when indexing many namespaces is slow

Removing per-request Init checks drops the stopping/stopped gate - when server.Stop sets initErr to stopping/stopped, handlers no longer call s.Init and requests keep being served against a stopped backend instead of failing fast
When a resource is written after its ListIterator snapshot during startup but before searchSupport.init calls WatchWriteEvents, the write is never replayed and the search index remains stale

Login-cache skip decision tests the org-aware wrapper (original) instead of the underlying model, causing it to miss real changes in login eligibility when an IDP linked to a disabled organization is updated (e.g. hideOnLogin). Both predicate tests return false, so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns early and login caches stay stale. After the organization is re-enabled, the hidden IDP can incorrectly reappear on the login page.

Test fixture creates one EC key without parameters (P-256) but tests claim to cover ES256, ES384, and ES512 which require P-256, P-384, and P-521 respectively - ES384/ES512 conversion and length handling for real signatures is untested

getBouncyCastleProvider returns whichever provider implements the default KeyStore type (normally SUN) instead of a Bouncy Castle provider, causing callers to resolve the wrong provider for BC-specific algorithms

integerToBytes does not reject negative values or values exceeding curve component width - it keeps only the last qLength bytes, silently transforming malformed DER components into different R/S values

Providers with same priority (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200) are silently selected based on ServiceLoader discovery order instead of being rejected or resolved deterministically
readInteger() does not verify that the INTEGER TLV consumes the entire decoder input - malformed signature components with extra bytes are accepted instead of rejected

ASN1 decoder compares only low five tag-number bits, accepting non-universal and incorrectly constructed/primitive tags (e.g. 0x70 as sequence or 0x82 as integer) instead of rejecting non-DER signatures
readInteger accepts any INTEGER byte string including negative values and non-minimal encodings without DER validation, allowing malformed values to be converted into valid-looking R||S signatures
Long-form length parser accepts non-DER encodings including long form for values below 128 and leading zero length octets instead of rejecting non-canonical DER encodings

Cleanup listener is gated on V1 flag, not on V2 being off - when both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and V2 feature are enabled, the event listener in AdminPermissions still handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent and calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which lands on ClientPermissionsV2 that throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing client deletion to fail

getClientsWithPermission returns the all-clients resource name as a client id - when an all-clients permission is granted, ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission iterates every resource of type Clients including the type-level resource named 'Clients', adding that literal name to the result as if it were a client id, causing callers that resolve ids to clients to hit a null client and fail

canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException on a reachable token-exchange path - when V2 is enabled and a client attempts token exchange, ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning an allow or deny decision, causing the token exchange request to fail with a server error

canView() ignores the MANAGE scope, unlike canView(ClientScopeModel) - when an admin holds only a MANAGE permission on all clients, ClientPermissionsV2.canView() returns false because it checks only canViewClientDefault() or the VIEW scope, causing canList() and requireView() to deny list and view calls even though canManage() is true

When updateStrategy is null, createInitialDeployment in UpgradeTest.java returns early before the FeatureSpec with rolling-updates is set, causing the default-strategy case of testCacheMaxCount to lack the required feature for gated update-compatibility commands, which may cause test failure or exercise the disabled path

canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, so view-only admins can manage groups - when an admin holds only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource, GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true because it checks VIEW and MANAGE, allowing management-guarded group operations for read-only admins

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs - it adds groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource UUID) instead of the group ID, causing group-scoped admins to get empty or incorrect results when listing/counting users

testManageGroupMembership test never verifies that the group-specific MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scope is required - the only negative assertion calls joinGroup("no-such") before any permission exists, and an implementation that ignores group permissions would still pass

GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions methods which are reachable through the GroupResource management-permissions endpoint, causing internal errors instead of controlled authorization errors when V2 is enabled

The account UI's i18next instance uses MessageFormat placeholders {0}, {1}, {2} and {2,choice,...} instead of i18next {{0}} style interpolation, causing raw placeholders to be displayed to users instead of actual values
The normalizeValue function in VerifyMessageProperties.java replaces entire ICU choice expressions with '...' before sanitization, allowing disallowed HTML inside choice branches to bypass validation
Lithuanian resource file messages_lt.properties contains Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' for totpStep1 instead of Lithuanian translation
Lithuanian login resource file messages_lt.properties contains Italian text for loginTotpStep1 instead of Lithuanian translation

English bundle path derivation uses replaceAll on absolute path which could incorrectly rewrite parent directories containing 'resources-community', and throws RuntimeException if derived _en file doesn't exist
Admin UI's messages_en.properties uses Java MessageFormat syntax {0}, {1}, {2} and {2,choice,...} instead of i18next {{0}} placeholders, causing literal template display instead of value substitution
Diff-trimming indices in verifySafeHtml can overlap when sanitized text differs by repeated characters, causing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of proper error reporting

isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong offsets - matchesSafely compares substring(3, 5) and returns false if it equals the expected shortcut, so correct IDs are not matched and wrong-grant IDs pass

AccessTokenContext constructor validates grantType a second time instead of validating rawTokenId, so a context with null rawTokenId is accepted and encodeTokenId later concatenates it as the literal string 'null'
Client credentials tokens never get a GRANT_TYPE attribute set on ClientSessionContext, so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider falls back to UNKNOWN and the 'cc' shortcut is never used

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory accepts any shortcut length from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory but the encoder/parser contract requires exactly two characters - custom grants with different length shortcuts will produce access-token IDs that cannot be decoded

When credential comes from getFederatedCredentialsStream(), the exhaustion path calls removeStoredCredentialById() which targets local/federated database store but does not delegate deletion to the external CredentialInputUpdater, leaving exhausted federated recovery-code credentials in place
Federated validation in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() only checks anyMatch and does not remove the used code, allowing the same recovery code to authenticate repeatedly indefinitely

When federated updater returns false, createRecoveryCodesCredential creates a local credential without accounting for existing federated recovery credential, causing newly generated local codes to be ignored while old federated codes continue to validate

When user.credentialManager().updateCredential returns true, createRecoveryCodesCredential skips recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential but leaves stale local recovery codes that may still validate

Adding recovery codes to isConfiguredFor makes provider report credential as configured, but disableCredentialType only clears OTP and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream omits recovery codes, leaving myUser.recoveryCodes intact after delete operation

The reader thread is never joined and its exceptions are only recorded asynchronously, so the assertion can run immediately after deletion before the thread has performed any read, allowing the test to pass without exercising the concurrent path and the thread can continue using managedRealm after the test has returned and its fixture is torn down

GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() returns null when the backing group was concurrently deleted, but the GroupModel contract explicitly guarantees that this method never returns null, which can cause unboxing failures or a null subgroup count in the REST output
getSubGroupsStream overloads dereference modelSupplier.get() without a null check, so a concurrent delete during sub-group listing still throws a NullPointerException
